newsitem.title: JAPAN: World watching how Japan economy performs - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: World watching how Japan economy performs - Rubin.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin told a news conference in Tokyo that he did not raise "specific components of macroeconomic policy" in his discussions on Friday with Japanese leaders.

But he said there was "enormous interest around the world" both in how the Japanese economy would perform and in "what additional strategies" Japan might take if it failed to meet its two objectives of maintaining domestic demand-led growth and avoiding a resurgence in its current account surplus.
Rubin added that he had no particular "benchmark" and no time frame for judging whether Japan had met those objectives.
Rubin said he did not think there was any question about Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's strong commitment to deregulation and economic growth in Japan.

"It strikes me as a very sound policy path to be on," he said. But he added that with regard to whether such policies would maintain domestic demand-led growth and avoid a resurgence of Japan's current account surplus: "I didn't mean to imply I was sanguine or not sanguine."
He said Japanese policy-makers saw no inconsistency between their fiscal consolidation policies and the growth and current-account objectives. "Obviously time will tell," Rubin said.
Rubin was visiting Tokyo for talks with Japanese government and business leaders on his way to a meeting of Asia-Pacific finance ministers in the Philippines.
